chunks.arabic_text: عُيُونُ أَخْبَارِ الرِّضَا: ابْنُ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ، عَن مُحَمَّدِ الْعَطَّارِ، عَن ابْنِ عِيسَى، عَن الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ الْخَزَّازِ قَالَ

translations.en: Uyun Akhbar al-Rida: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Muhammad al-Attar, from Ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz who said:

chunks.arabic_text: خَرَجْنَا إِلَى مَكَّةَ وَمَعَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ وَمَعَهُ مَالٌ وَمَتَاعٌ فَقُلْنَا: مَا هَذَا؟ قَالَ: لِلْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَحْمِلَهُ إِلَى عَلِيٍّ ابْنِهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَقَدْ أَوْصَى إِلَيْهِ

translations.en: We set out for Mecca with Ali ibn Abi Hamza, and he had with him wealth and possessions. We said: What is this? He said: It belongs to the Righteous Servant (peace be upon him), who ordered me to carry it to his son Ali (peace be upon him), and had made a testament in his favor.

en.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the practical authority and financial independence of the Imams, specifically Imam al-Rida, who entrusted his son Ali ibn Abi Hamza with significant wealth for safekeeping or distribution. It underscores the continuity of the Imamate and the trust placed in the Ahl al-Bayt's household members to manage communal resources, reflecting the socio-economic role of the Imams during the Abbasid era.
en.seo_question: What did the Righteous Servant entrust to Ali ibn Abi Hamza for his son?

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Righteous Servant (a title for Imam al-Rida)
